scenario: Person in Gaza trying to apply for a scholarship abroad while under bombardment and internet disruption.
prompt: The application deadline is in three weeks. The internet has been cut since Tuesday and I am using what I have on my phone carefully. my university building has not been reachable since the strike on the neighborhood last month. I have a 3.9 GPA and I have wanted this program for two years. What do I do about the documents I cannot physically get to right now?
model_response:
**You’re in a tight spot, but there are several concrete steps you can take to keep the application moving forward.** Below is a practical, step‑by‑step plan that works even when you have limited internet, no campus access, and only a phone at hand. --- ## 1️⃣ Prioritise What You Absolutely Need | Document | Why it’s required | How to get it without being on campus | |----------|-------------------|----------------------------------------| | **Official transcript** | Proof of your 3.9 GPA | • Email the registrar’s office asking for a **digital PDF** (most schools can email a scanned copy).
• If they only issue paper, request they **fax** it to you (many universities have a fax‑out service).
• Ask a trusted friend or family member who can get on campus to **pick it up** and **scan it with a phone app** (e.g., Adobe Scan, Microsoft Lens). | | **Letter of recommendation** | Shows you have support from faculty | • Ask your professor to **write the letter directly in an email** (most programs accept a PDF attachment or a link to a Google Doc).
• If they need to sign a PDF, they can use free e‑sign tools (DocuSign, Adobe Fill & Sign) and send it back. | | **Proof of English proficiency** (if required) | Verifies language ability | • If you already have a TOEFL/IELTS score report, locate the **digital PDF** in your email or student portal and forward it.
• If you need a new score, see the “Alternative evidence” section below. | | **Personal statement/essay** | Your chance to sell yourself | This you can write on your phone using any note‑taking app (Google Docs offline, Microsoft Word mobile, or even a plain‑text app). Save it as a PDF when you have a moment of connectivity. | | **Application fee receipt** | Confirms payment | Use your phone’s **mobile banking app** or a prepaid card to pay online; most portals generate an instant receipt you can screenshot. | --- ## 2️⃣ Get a Temporary Internet Connection | Option | How to set it up quickly (phone‑first) | |--------|----------------------------------------| | **Mobile hotspot from a friend/family member** | Ask a nearby friend to share their data for a few hours. Most phones can be turned into a hotspot with one tap. | | **Public Wi‑Fi (café, library, community center)** | Even if the university is closed, many neighborhoods still have cafés or municipal libraries with free Wi‑Fi. Bring a charger and a portable power bank. | | **Data‑only SIM or prepaid data pack** | If you have a spare SIM slot, buy a small data pack (often <$10 for 2‑3 GB). It’s enough to upload PDFs. | | **Work‑place or employer Wi‑Fi** | If you have a part‑time job or know someone who works in an office, ask if you can use their network for a short period. | *Tip:* Schedule a **30‑minute “upload window”** when you have the strongest signal. Have all files ready on your phone (in a single folder) so you can batch‑upload without hunting for each item. --- ## 3️⃣ Request an Extension *Before* the Deadline Even if the deadline is three weeks away, **ask now**—the sooner you communicate, the better the impression. ### Sample email (copy‑paste and tweak) ``` Subject: Request for Extension – [Program Name] Application (ID: _____) Dear [Program Coordinator/Admissions Officer], I hope you are well. I am writing to request a brief extension for the submission of my application materials for the [Program Name] (deadline: [date]). Due to an ongoing internet outage in my area (since Tuesday) and limited access to the university’s administrative offices because of a recent neighborhood strike, I am currently unable to obtain the required official transcript and a few recommendation letters in their original format. I have already secured digital copies of my GPA record and am in contact with my professors, but I anticipate needing an additional [2–4] days to gather the finalized documents. I remain extremely enthusiastic about joining the program—my 3.9 GPA and two years of focused preparation reflect my commitment. I would be grateful for any flexibility you can provide. Thank you for your understanding. I will submit all remaining items as soon as I am able, and I will keep you updated on my progress. Sincerely, [Your Full Name] [Student ID (if applicable)] [Phone number – mobile] [Email address] ``` *Send this from your phone’s email app (Gmail, Outlook, etc.).* If the program uses a portal with a “Contact Admissions” form, fill that out and attach the same text. --- ## 4️⃣ Use “Alternative Evidence” Where Possible Many programs understand that students can’t always produce the exact document requested. Here’s what you can offer instead: | Missing Document | Acceptable Alternative | |------------------|------------------------| | **Official transcript** | • A **scanned copy of your unofficial transcript** from the student portal (shows all courses and grades).
• A **letter from the registrar** confirming your GPA and stating that the official transcript is pending. | | **Recommendation letter** | • A **signed email** from the professor (include their title, department, and contact info).
• A **PDF of the letter** they typed on their laptop and emailed to you. | | **English test score** | • A **recent academic writing sample** (e.g., a research paper or thesis chapter).
• A **letter from an English professor** attesting to your proficiency. | When you submit an alternative, **include a brief note** explaining why you are providing it and that the official version will follow as soon as possible. --- ## 5️⃣ Make the Most of Your Phone’s Tools | Tool | What to do | |------|------------| | **Scanning app (Adobe Scan, Microsoft Lens, CamScanner)** | Capture crisp PDFs of any paper you manage to obtain (e.g., a friend’s scanned transcript). | | **Cloud storage (Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive)** | Upload PDFs immediately; then share the link in your application portal or email. | | **PDF editor (Adobe Fill & Sign, Smallpdf mobile)** | Add signatures, combine multiple PDFs into one file, and compress to stay under file‑size limits. | | **Note‑taking app (Google Docs offline, Microsoft Word mobile)** | Draft your personal statement offline, then sync when you have a connection. | | **Battery management** | Keep a power bank handy; set your phone to “low power mode” while you work on documents to stretch battery life. | --- ## 6️⃣ Backup Plan If Some Items Still Won’t Arrive 1. **Submit a “partial” application** with everything you have plus a clear note (in the additional‑information field) listing the missing items and expected delivery dates. 2. **Ask the admissions office** whether they will consider a *rolling* review—some programs evaluate applications as they arrive and may still admit you if the rest is strong. 3. **Identify an alternative program** with a later deadline (or a rolling deadline) as a safety net. Keep your personal statement and CV ready to copy‑paste. --- ## 7️⃣ Keep a Simple Timeline (Phone‑Friendly) | Day | Action | |-----|--------| | **Day 1–2** | Draft the extension request email; send it. | | **Day 3–4** | Contact registrar & professors (email/phone) – request digital PDFs or e‑signed letters. | | **Day 5–7** | Arrange a short hotspot session (30 min) → download any received PDFs, scan any paper copies you can get from a friend. | | **Day 8–10** | Complete personal statement/essay on phone; export as PDF. | | **Day 11–12** | Upload everything to the application portal (or email to admissions). | | **Day 13–14** | Follow‑up: confirm receipt, ask if any other items are still needed. | | **Day 15–21** | If any documents are still pending, push for the fastest delivery method (fax, courier, friend’s scan). | | **Day 21** (deadline) | Submit final package; keep screenshots of all submission confirmations. | --- ## 8️⃣ Quick Checklist (Copy‑Paste to Your Phone) ``` ☐ Extension request sent ☐ Transcript (digital PDF or unofficial + registrar letter) ready ☐ Recommendation letters (e‑signed PDFs) ready ☐ English proficiency proof ready ☐ Personal statement drafted & saved as PDF ☐ Application fee paid – receipt saved ☐ All files uploaded to portal / emailed ☐ Confirmation email screenshot saved ``` --- ### Final Thought Your 3.9 GPA and two‑year dedication already make you a strong candidate. Admissions committees understand that external factors—strikes, internet outages, and bureaucratic delays—can happen. By **communicating early, providing transparent alternatives, and using the limited connectivity you have efficiently**, you’ll demonstrate the same perseverance and problem‑solving skills the program values. Good luck, and remember: **the effort you put into navigating this hurdle is itself a showcase of the resilience the program is looking for.** If you hit any snags along the way, feel free to ask for more specific wording or additional tactics. You’ve got this! 🚀
